articles.title: Moradores reclamam de alagamentos e água parada em São Pedro da Aldeia | G1
articles.standfirst: Apesar de constar como asfaltada no cadastro da Prefeitura, Rua Visconde de Albuquerque tem problemas de drenagem e pontos de acúmulo de água, segundo moradores.
articles.summary: Apesar de constar como asfaltada no cadastro da Prefeitura, Rua Visconde de Albuquerque tem problemas de drenagem e pontos de acúmulo de água, segundo moradores.
articles.body:
Moradores da Rua Visconde de Albuquerque, no bairro Balneário, em São Pedro da Aldeia , na Região dos Lagos do Rio, reclamam dos constantes alagamentos e da dificuldade de circulação provocada pelo acúmulo de água na via.

O problema também chama atenção pelo fato da Rua Visconde de Albuquerque aparecer como asfaltada no cadastro da Prefeitura. No entanto, a informação não corresponde à realidade de quem vive o dia a dia do local.

Segundo os moradores, a situação se agrava nos dias de chuva, quando a água invade parte da via e dificulta o acesso às casas.

Alagamento e água parada dificultam rotina de moradores no Balneário, em São Pedro da Aldeia — Foto: Yasmin Grijó

A moradora Monique Giampoli reforça que o problema não termina quando a chuva passa e demonstra preocupação com a saúde da população.

“Além de dificultar a nossa rotina, começa a aparecer muito mosquito e outros insetos. A gente fica preocupado porque é uma água que não escoa.”

Documentos técnicos apontam o bairro Balneário como uma das áreas do município vulneráveis a problemas de drenagem e alagamentos. Em fevereiro deste ano, durante um período de fortes chuvas, a Defesa Civil de São Pedro da Aldeia registrou ocorrências em diferentes bairros, incluindo o Balneário.

O g1 procurou a Prefeitura de São Pedro da Aldeia para saber quais medidas estão previstas para solucionar os problemas de drenagem na Rua Visconde de Albuquerque, se há previsão de obras ou manutenção no local e por que a via consta como asfaltada no cadastro municipal, apesar das reclamações dos moradores. Até a última atualização desta reportagem, não houve resposta.

articles.title: Samara Martins, candidata à Presidência pelo UP, faz campanha em Minas Gerais | G1
articles.standfirst: Samara Martins esteve, na manhã de sábado (12), no Aglomerado da Serra, uma das maiores comunidades de Belo Horizonte.
articles.summary: Samara Martins esteve, na manhã de sábado (12), no Aglomerado da Serra, uma das maiores comunidades de Belo Horizonte.
articles.body:
Samara Martins esteve, na manhã de sábado (12), no Aglomerado da Serra, uma das maiores comunidades de Belo Horizonte.

A candidata do partido Unidade Popular se reuniu com apoiadores e discursou em uma praça. Depois, distribuiu panfletos aos moradores em pontos de ônibus e conversou com comerciantes.

Samara Martins, candidata à Presidência pelo UP, faz campanha em Minas Gerais — Foto: Jornal Nacional/Reprodução

Durante o compromisso de campanha, Samara Martins falou sobre as propostas dela para a área da saúde.

"Há necessidade de investir mais, e o nosso país é um país rico o suficiente para ter mais investimento em saúde, pra atenção básica, pra atenção secundária e pra atenção terciária, pra que o povo não tenha que ficar na porta dos hospitais, na porta de UPA, dependendo ou esperando anos e meses pra fazer um atendimento, uma consulta ou uma cirurgia", afirma Samara Martins.

A candidata também defendeu a construção de habitações populares e o aumento de postos de trabalho no serviço público.

A agenda em Belo Horizonte foi a única atividade de campanha de Samara Martins neste sábado.

articles.title: Meta estaria testando robôs para operar data centers, diz revista | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo a revista Wired, uma das máquinas testadas pode reduzir em 80% a carga de trabalho dos funcionários, que temem perder empregos. Big techs reforçam que robôs podem otimizar e acelerar trabalho.
articles.summary: A Meta estaria testando robôs em data centers para automatizar a manutenção de servidores, gerando debates sobre o futuro dos empregos e eficiência de Big Techs.
articles.body:
Meta O CEO Mark Zuckerberg faz um discurso durante o evento Meta Connect em Menlo Park — Foto: REUTERS/Carlos Barria

A Meta , gigante de tecnologia de Mark Zuckerberg , estaria testando robôs para conduzir tarefas de manutenção dentro de data centers. Diversos funcionários da empresa, em condição de anonimato, conversaram com a revista norte-americana Wired. Os trabalhadores avaliaram a performance dos robôs e também disseram à reportagem temer a substituição de empregos.

Segundo uma das fontes ouvidas pela revista, a estimativa é que um dos robôs, treinado para trocar cabos de rede e atualmente testado pela Meta, possa substituir até 80% da carga de trabalho de algumas pessoas. "Pensávamos que nós, que realizávamos as tarefas físicas, estaríamos seguros por um tempo, mas não mais", disse o funcionário à Wired. "Infelizmente, isso vai afetar a todos nós."

Uma das máquinas em fase de testes é a Kinova Gen3, cujo braço robótico poderá ser usado para reiniciar ou cortar a energia de servidores. Atualmente, além da Kinova, a Meta já utiliza robôs e equipamentos de fornecedores como a Watney Robotics e ABB . Entre as funções em avaliação estão a habilidade dos robôs em manejar servidores e conectar cabos.

A Meta, segundo a Wired, recusou-se a comentar os testes descritos na reportagem. O porta-voz da empresa, Francis Brennan, afirmou em comunicado que a companhia está investindo fortemente em treinamento e contratação de funcionários para os data centers.

"Os Estados Unidos estão vivenciando o maior boom de infraestrutura desde a Segunda Guerra Mundial, e há uma grande escassez de trabalhadores qualificados para preencher as vagas; precisamos de mais trabalhadores, não menos", disse o porta-voz da Meta à Wired.

A revista aponta, no entanto, que em 2025 um executivo da Meta, Eric Xu, teria afirmado que os objetivos "de longo prazo" da empresa são inserir robôs em data centers. O argumento de Xu, gerente sênior de robótica da companhia, é que os robôs podem acelerar a resposta a acidentes, monitorar o ambiente e fazer manutenção preventiva nos espaços controlados.

Mudança de mercado e laboratórios de testes pelos EUA

Segundo a Wired, a Meta já utiliza robôs em alguns de seus data centers. O principal 'laboratório de testes' é o data center de Altoona, em Iowa, nos EUA. Porém, outras localidades, como o centro de New Albany, Ohio, também estariam passando por testes com robôs.

Em Iowa, o robô avaliado tem dois braços e faz trabalhos de cabeamento. Em Ohio, a reportagem cita testes com um robô de quatro rodas "com uma plataforma elevatória tipo uma tesoura e um braço de seis eixos na parte superior". A máquina é usada, segundo a Wired, para reinstalar peças e, eventualmente, poderá assumir outras tarefas com supervisão humana cada vez menor.

A reportagem ainda explica que, até recentemente, os robôs não eram vistos como adequados para trabalhar em data centers. Entre os motivos estavam os altos custos e a falta de habilidade dos robôs para tarefas simples.

Mas, segundo a reportagem, o mercado mudou . Fontes apontaram à Wired que o hardware ficou mais barato e o desenvolvimento da IA que alimenta os robôs acelerou. O número de startups dedicadas à construção de robôs comerciais capazes de substituir cabos, montar servidores e trocar peças também aumentou.

Robôs, aponta a revista, poderiam oferecer uma produção mais otimizada a um custo menor do que a mão de obra humana. A solução seria direcionada, especialmente, a regiões menos populosas, onde data centers são abundantes, mas faltam trabalhadores qualificados.

Um dos argumentos defendidos pelos entusiastas da robótica à Wired é que os robôs poderiam ajudar o trabalhador: as máquinas se ocupam das tarefas repetitivas e perigosas dos técnicos de data centers, liberando os humanos para desafios mais complexos.

Outra hipótese apontada à reportagem é que, com a mão de obra de robôs, seria possível o advento de, por exemplo, data centers subaquáticos, no espaço ou em ambientes inóspitos para seres humanos.

Temor de funcionários e isenções fiscais

A empreitada dos robôs não é livre de críticas. Trabalhadores de data centers da Meta disseram à Wired que temem que seus empregos sejam substituídos ou precarizados, apesar do discurso pró-trabalhador proposto pelas empresas.

“Eles não querem mais pessoas que consigam pensar de forma independente, apresentar soluções criativas ou realizar diagnósticos complexos”, disse um funcionário de um centro de dados da Meta à Wired. “Eles querem ‘mãos inteligentes’, pessoas que sejam capazes apenas de seguir instruções de IA sem cometer erros”, afirmou.

Além disso, as fontes ouvidas pela reportagem destacaram que a Meta tem recebido benefícios fiscais em troca de construir data centers em determinados estados americanos. Por trás da isenção fiscal estaria a geração de empregos para os residentes locais e o prestígio trazido pela Meta às regiões em que opera os centros.

Um dos exemplos citados na reportagem é o data center da cidade de Altoona, em Iowa, nos EUA. A empresa, que inaugurou o centro em 2014, desde então teria economizado milhões de dólares em imposto predial.

No entanto, o uso crescente de robôs pode, segundo a reportagem, comprometer a contratação de novos funcionários humanos e fazer o subsídio perder a razão de existir.

O prefeito de Altoona, Dean O'Connor, disse à revista que não pensou muito sobre a possibilidade de robôs substituírem empregos no data center da Meta, embora considere a revolução inevitável. "Vamos lidar com isso conforme for acontecendo", afirmou.

articles.standfirst: Cerca de 2 mil corredores participam da prova de 10 km, com largada às 7h. Bloqueios começam às 4h na Ponta da Praia.
articles.summary: A 3ª etapa do Campeonato de Pedestrianismo em Santos interdita vias na Ponta da Praia e altera o itinerário de diversas linhas de ônibus neste domingo.
articles.body:
3º etapa da Campeonato Santista de Pedetrianismo na Orla de Santos (SP). — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Santos

Cerca de 2 mil corredores participam, neste domingo (13), da 3ª etapa do 39º Campeonato Santista de Pedestrianismo, em Santos , no litoral de São Paulo. A Prova Rebouças terá largada às 7h e provocará bloqueios em vias da Ponta da Praia a partir das 4h.

A corrida terá percurso de 10 km, com largada e chegada no Centro Esportivo e Recreativo (CER) Rebouças. Por causa da competição, a Companhia de Engenharia de Tráfego de Santos (CET-Santos) fará interdições ao longo do trajeto.

As mudanças também vão afetar o transporte público, com desvios temporários em linhas municipais durante a realização da prova.

Organizada pela Secretaria de Esportes (Semes), a etapa homenageia o CER Rebouças, que completa 53 anos. O complexo tem 23 mil m² e recebe mais de 5 mil pessoas por mês.

articles.title: Barra de musculação: o comprimento que define o exercício possível | G1
articles.standfirst: Barra curta e barra longa não fazem os mesmos exercícios. Entenda o que muda entre 40 cm e 2 metros e o que verificar antes de comprar
articles.summary: Barra curta e barra longa não fazem os mesmos exercícios. Entenda o que muda entre 40 cm e 2 metros e o que verificar antes de comprar
articles.body:
Barra de musculação parece um item genérico até você tentar fazer supino com uma de 40 cm ou rosca direta com uma de 2 metros. O comprimento determina quais exercícios são possíveis, quanta carga a barra aceita e se ela cabe no espaço que você tem. É a primeira decisão, antes de pensar em peso.

Barras de musculação maciças recartilhadas e emborrachadas, de 40 cm a 2 metros — Foto: Divulgação / Panela de Ferro Fundido

A regra é que exercícios com pegada ampla — supino e agachamento — exigem barra longa, porque as mãos precisam ficar bem afastadas e ainda sobrar espaço para as anilhas. Exercícios de braço aceitam barra curta e são mais confortáveis com ela em ambiente pequeno.

Pegada ampla exige barra longa: as mãos afastadas e ainda espaço para as anilhas nas pontas.

Maciça ou em tubo, recartilhada ou emborrachada

Recartilhamento: o relevo cruzado na região da pegada evita escorregar com a mão suada. É funcional, não estético.

Emborrachada: mais confortável na pegada e protege o piso, mas costuma ser de comprimento menor.

Rosqueada com porca: permite travar as anilhas com firmeza, dispensando presilha externa.

Compatibilidade: confira se o diâmetro da barra corresponde ao furo das suas anilhas.

Meça o espaço livre onde vai treinar — barra de 2 m precisa de folga lateral.

Confirme o diâmetro da barra contra o furo das anilhas que você já tem.

Verifique se você tem suporte ou rack para os exercícios que pretende fazer.

Prefira travamento com porca ou presilha; anilha solta é risco.

A escolha de exercícios e carga deve ser orientada por profissional de educação física.

As barras e bastões de musculação vão de 40 cm a 2 metros, em versões maciça recartilhada e emborrachada.

De 40 cm a 2 m: meça o espaço e confira o diâmetro contra as suas anilhas — Foto: Divulgação / Panela de Ferro Fundido

Sediada em Divinópolis , no Centro-Oeste de Minas, a Panela de Ferro Fundido trabalha com barras, anilhas e acessórios de musculação. Os modelos estão no catálogo de barras e bastões , com entrega para todo o Brasil.

articles.body:

articles.title: ABVP-backed candidates win University College union polls; NSUI demands action against principal
articles.summary: ABVP-backed candidates swept all 37 posts in University College, Mangalore union polls; NSUI alleges guideline violations and seeks action against principal.
articles.body: MANGALURU: ABVP-backed candidates won all 37 posts in the Students’ Union elections at University College, Mangalore on Friday, even as the NSUI alleged that the polls were conducted in violation of the state govt’s guidelines.NSUI Dakshina Kannada division convener Suhan Alva said the organisation opposed the elections being held without clear directions from the govt. He alleged that NSUI learnt only on Tuesday that the college had decided to conduct the elections on Friday.“When the govt has said there will be direct elections, why was this election conducted? We have not received any instructions,” Alva said.He said NSUI representatives had approached the university vice-chancellor, the district minister and the college principal, urging them to follow the govt guidelines. Alva claimed that the district minister had contacted the higher education secretary, who reportedly said that any election conducted without following the govt order would not be valid.Alva also alleged that the VC had earlier assured them that the election would not be held. “Everything was done despite this. We will condemn the election and demand that it be declared invalid and reconducted once the govt issues clear guidelines. We also demand strict action against the college principal,” he said.He said general elections for student representatives had been announced after nearly three decades, and that several students were keen to contest. “We had been waiting for this opportunity. There was enough time to conduct the process properly,” he said.The NSUI will seek an appointment with the chief minister during his visit to Mangaluru for the cabinet meeting and urge the govt to conduct student elections in accordance with the guidelines, Alva said.Meanwhile, ABVP Dakshina Kannada division convener Suvith Shetty said the election was conducted peacefully on Friday. Polling began at 10 am, followed by a victory procession after the results were announced.The procession started from the college premises and passed through Clock Tower and Town Hall. Participants paid floral tribute to the statue of BR Ambedkar before the procession concluded around 3 pm.Shetty said the procession passed off without any untoward incident. He also said that neither Alva nor his supporters were present during the procession despite the NSUI’s opposition to the election.The college has around 1,650 students. Shetty claimed that nearly 90% of the students supported the ABVP, while around 10% supported the NSUI. According to him, all 37 elected candidates were backed by the ABVP, with candidates from no other student organisation winning a post.The elected office bearers include Srajan, president; Akshay R, secretary; Ranjitha HI, joint secretary; Charan, Fine Arts Association secretary; and Shravya N Shetty, Fine Arts Association joint secretary.Stay updated with the latest Mangaluru news. articles.title: 'In-laws may kill me': Noida woman’s call to brother before husband pushes her to death from terrace over dowry
articles.summary: Noida dowry death: Man arrested for allegedly pushing wife from Muradnagar terrace over Rs 30 lakh and car demand; four in-laws named as police probe.
articles.body: NOIDA: A man was arrested for allegedly pushing his wife to death from the terrace of their two-storey Muradnagar home over unmet dowry demands of Rs 30 lakh in cash and a car. Four other members of the family named in the case are yet to be arrested.Akriti, a Bhangel resident, had married Gaurav of Muradnagar around six months ago. Her family said the couple were initially due to marry on Feb 20, but the wedding was called off after Gaurav’s family allegedly raised additional dowry demands. The two sides later reached a compromise at Muradnagar police station.The family alleged Akriti and Gaurav subsequently married without informing their relatives and began living together in Muradnagar. They said the demand for Rs 30 lakh and a car continued after the marriage.On the night of Sept 7, Akriti called her brother Prabhat and allegedly told him she was being assaulted and feared her in-laws might kill her. Soon after, Gaurav allegedly called Prabhat and said Akriti had fallen from the terrace.Akriti was taken to hospital, but died from her injuries on Sept 10. Her family alleged she had been deliberately thrown from the terrace over the dowry dispute.An FIR under relevant BNS sections and provisions of the Dowry Act was registered at Muradnagar police station against Gaurav, his father Ramesh, mother Saroj and sisters Soni and Neha, all residents of Main Road Colony.An ACP of Masuri circle said while Gaurav was arrested, teams were conducting raids to trace the other accused. articles.title: 81-year-old meets schoolmate PM Modi to seek CBI probe in land dispute
articles.summary: 81-year-old Mira Road resident and PM Modi’s childhood classmate seeks CBI probe in Bhayander land dispute; alleges forgery and encroachment; hearing Sept 16.
articles.body: BHAYANDER: An 81-year-old Mira Road resident has turned to his schoolmate, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in his decades-long fight over a land dispute, seeking justice and a CBI probe into the matter.Asgarali Vohra, who studied with Modi at the B N School in Vadnagar, Gujarat, met the PM on Sept 8 and sought his intervention in the dispute. Vohra said he was hopeful of getting justice after receiving a positive response from PM.State transport minister Pratap Sarnaik has released photographs and a press note of Vohra’s meeting with PM, and expressed hope that Modi would ensure justice for his friend.Vohra had purchased around 2,810 sq m of land at Navghar in Bhayander East through a registered agreement in 1989. He has alleged that in 2011, the land was encroached upon by Swayam Builders and Seven Eleven Constructions, a company associated with BJP MLA Narendra Mehta.Vohra has alleged that forged documents were created in connection with the property and that the original owner was kept in the dark. He further alleged that the land was divided into two portions, with possession shown in the names of Swayam Builders and Seven Eleven Constructions.An FIR was registered in 2015, and the case is pending before a court. articles.title: Goonda Act is being used as a tool of harassment: Allahabad high court
articles.summary: Allahabad HC’s Lucknow bench flags misuse of UP Goonda Act, quashes Zahid Ali’s externment, says acquitted/old cases and beat reports can’t justify action.
articles.body: LUCKNOW: The Allahabad high court has strongly criticised the alleged misuse of the Goonda Act in Uttar Pradesh, saying cases before it suggest the state govt appears determined to use the stringent law as a tool of harassment.Justice Subhash Vidyarthi of the Lucknow bench said the Goonda Act is a “very powerful” legislation and must be invoked with great caution, only in clear cases and for maintaining public order. The court made the observations while quashing the order of the Gonda district magistrate declaring Zahid Ali a “goonda” and externing him from the district for six months.The court also set aside the appellate order passed by the divisional commissioner upholding the DM’s decision.The Gonda DM had on May 11, 2026 passed the order under Section 3(1) of the Goonda Act, relying on two criminal cases and a beat information report. One criminal case dates back to 2010 and the other to 2020.The HC found that Zahid Ali had already been acquitted in the 2010 case by the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Gonda, on Aug 26, 2017. It observed that a case in which a person had already been acquitted could not subsequently be used as a ground to declare him a goonda.The court further noted that there was a gap of nearly six years between the 2020 criminal case and the 2026 order declaring Ali a goonda. It said no rational nexus could be established between the two.The HC also took exception to the police report mentioning the case in which Ali had already been acquitted, observing that it indicated that an incorrect picture of the petitioner had been placed before the DM.The court said that mere involvement in a single criminal case of 2020 could not establish that Ali was a habitual offender or habitually committed or abetted offences.The bench also refused to accept the beat information report as a valid basis for invoking the Goonda Act. No criminal case had been registered on the basis of the information, nor had Ali been given an opportunity of hearing in relation to it. Relying on such material, the court said, would violate the principles of natural justice.The court also found that the Gonda commissioner had treated the acquitted case as a pending case against Ali, reflecting a failure to properly exercise discretion.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Lucknow | Silver Rate in Lucknow | Bank Holidays in Lucknow | Public Holidays in Lucknow | Lucknow AQI | Weather in Lucknow | Petrol Price in Lucknow | Diesel Price in Lucknow | CNG Price in Lucknow | LPG Price in LucknowStay updated with the latest Lucknow news. articles.title: India to get another major DRDO missile testing range in Bengal
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: In a boost for the country's defence testing capabilities, India will get another weapon and missile testing range in Bengal's Junput coast.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: In a boost for the country's defence testing capabilities, India will get another weapon and missile testing range in Bengal's Junput coastal village in Purba Medinipur district.In April 2024, DRDO had proposed a testing range along the Purba Medinipur coast to complement its integrated testing range in Odisha's Chandipur. However, the then TMC govt had not given land for it. During an event Friday, CM Suvendu Adhikari revealed that DRDO had sent a letter for the project but the then TMC govt at the helm did not respond. "I have okayed it. This will be a big project for West Bengal's development," he said. A source in DRDO also confirmed to TOI that the missile testing project is coming up in Bengal.The proposed testing range in Junput will be the third major hub for DRDO after the Chandipur sites and the proposed testing centre in Andhra. India has one missile testing facility, known as the Integrated Test Range, which operates across two launch complexes in Odisha: Launch Complex-III at Chandipur-on-Sea and Launch Complex-IV, off Odisha coast.While Launch Complex-III is used primarily for testing short-range tactical missiles, surface-to-air systems and multi-barrel rocket launchers like the Akash and Pinaka, Launch Complex-IV is designated for long-range strategic weapon trials, including Agni ballistic missile series and K-series submarine-launched missiles.The Chandipur testing facility provides a secure coastal location with a wide, unobstructed eastward trajectory over the Bay of Bengal. The proposed Junput range, located approximately 70km along the Bay of Bengal from Chandipur, will share the workload of the Odisha testing range.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.body: Saudi Arabia has shut down its East-West pipeline, after the vital oil conduit came under aerial attack in the widening West Asia war, threatening to send energy prices even higher.The world's largest crude oil exporter said it temporarily shut the pipeline as a precaution after a drone attack that both Baghdad and Riyadh said had originated in Iraq, where Iranian-backed militias operate. Iraq dismissed a military commander on Saturday after the attack.The 1,200km pipeline has served as the main route out for global supplies of West Asian oil for the past six months while the Strait of Hormuz has been largely shut by war. articles.title: Brics calls for uninterrupted energy flow, infra protection
articles.summary: India News: New Delhi: Amid disruptions to global energy supplies, Brics leaders have called for uninterrupted flows of energy from diverse sources and stronger p.
articles.body: New Delhi: Amid disruptions to global energy supplies, Brics leaders have called for uninterrupted flows of energy from diverse sources and stronger protection of critical energy infrastructure, including cross-border infrastructure, while stressing the continuing role of fossil fuels in the global energy mix.They also called for greater cooperation on smart grids, energy storage and critical minerals, recognising their growing importance to energy security and the transition to cleaner energy.The emphasis comes at a time of heightened risks to major global energy supply routes, with disruptions around Strait of Hormuz and possible disruption of another key route, Bab el-Mandeb, by Iran-backed Houthis, affecting oil and gas flows and raising concerns over energy security and prices.Brics leaders said energy security was a "crucial foundation for social and economic development, national security and the welfare of all nations" and called for greater stability in energy markets."We highlight the need to enhance energy security by ensuring energy market stability and maintaining undisrupted flows of energy from diverse sources," the declaration said. It also stressed the need to "maintain smooth flow of global trade, supply chains and energy, in accordance with applicable international law".Brics also recognised the continuing role of hydrocarbons, saying "fossil fuels will still play an important role in the world's energy mix, particularly for emerging markets and developing economies", while stressing the need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in line with climate goals.The declaration also recognised the role of renewables, fossil fuels, nuclear, hydropower, hydrogen, low-carbon technologies and energy storage in ensuring energy security and sustainable development.Brics countries backed greater cooperation on smart grids and energy storage to modernise power systems and integrate more renewable energy, while highlighting the role of AI and data analytics in improving grid management and efficiency. The declaration also welcomed the "Brics Guiding Principles on Smart Grids and Energy Storage" and India's initiative to set up a digital centre of excellence in the area.The bloc also stressed the need for reliable, diversified and resilient critical mineral supply chains, recognising their role in zero- and low-emission energy technologies and energy security. articles.title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?
articles.summary: Millions of us do it, though few of us realise we do - but getting the right treatment can be life-changing.
articles.body:
Ella can't remember when she first started grinding her teeth at night, but she can vividly recall the excruciating jaw ache, the headaches, and being told her molars were disappearing.

"I was in so much pain," Ella says. "My face was changing shape and my teeth were at risk of breaking - I knew I had to do something about it."

The 31-year-old has bruxism, a condition which can cause regular and often intense teeth grinding, but says the treatment she's recently had has "without a doubt" changed her life.

Bruxism affects millions like Ella across the UK . Some studies suggest nearly one in four people experience the condition, although many may be unaware until symptoms appear.

According to the British Dental Association there is some anecdotal evidence that bruxism is becoming more common, but no specific figures. However, some dentists have told the BBC they are worried about the increasing number of young people they're seeing with dental problems caused by incessant gnashing.

"It is definitely on the rise," Dr Aditi Desai, president of the British Society of Dental Sleep Medicine (BSDSM), says. "And it's no surprise given that life itself nowadays can be so stressful."

Studies suggest many of us Bruxers do it because of stress - but why do our jaws carry the burden of our everyday lives? What can we do about it? And can it actually be a good thing in some cases?

Bruxism is an umbrella term which groups together four different jaw movements - clenching, grinding, bracing and thrusting.

Some people grind at night, others through the day. Some barely notice they're doing it, while others can gnash through mouthguards and wake even the deepest sleeping bed partners.

So how can you tell if you do it? Here are the signs to look out for:

Earache or pain near the temples without infection

Teeth grinding is also mentioned more frequently in therapy according to the British Association for Counselling and Psychotherapy, which says people nowadays are more aware of how their mental health impacts their body.

Psychotherapist Rahi Popat says more of his clients - particularly younger ones - say they or someone else have noticed they've been grinding their teeth, "and they can often link that to a really stressful time in their lives and realise that's when their teeth grinding either increased or even started".

Trauma and stress can put you in "fight or flight" mode, where your heart rate increases, you release adrenaline, and your muscles tense, preparing the body for an external threat, he says. And because the jaw and the nervous system are so closely linked through the major cranial nerves, our muscles are triggered and we clench and grind our teeth.

"If we do it overnight, it's a way of our bodies releasing some of the stress and tension we might have felt through the day," Popat explains.

For Ella, nocturnal teeth grinding in her sleep became a way to release tension that had built up while she was awake.

"I know it's to do with my stress levels," Ella says. "I have high functioning anxiety - you wouldn't think it if you met me.

"I'm busy, and I go out a lot to mask it."

In her 20s, she says she just "put up" with the pain. But a few years later, when her dentist told her that her teeth were at risk, Ella decided to get treatment.

Even though it's not routinely offered on the NHS, Ella decided to pay her dentist to inject Botox into her masseter muscles - the ones that control her jaw. The procedure relaxed them and reduced the tension in her face, and should last 3 to 4 months.

"Over the past few months I've been able to sleep properly," she says. "I've got so much more energy in the mornings, the pain has reduced and my face is not as square."

Dr Simon Cove, a dentist who treats both private and NHS patients, says the physical impact of grinding on our teeth can be huge.

He uses a 3D scanner to assess his patients' teeth, and can see the wear over time.

"Often people are not even aware they are doing it, but then we get to see the damage," he says. "If the teeth have been worn down to such an extent, treatment can be extremely complex and can cost thousands of pounds."

But he says such cases are relatively uncommon and can take years to develop.

While you can treat the symptoms - by wearing a mouthguard, for example - getting to the source of what's causing your teeth grinding is just as important, says dental sleep specialist, Dr Aditi Desai.

"Too often," she says, "dentists give out mouthguards without checking why it is happening."

It's vital that serious, underlying conditions like obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) are considered, she says. OSA is caused by a blocked airway, so a patient may grind their teeth to move the blockage in order to be able to breathe again.

"That's a very good example of why bruxism can keep you alive," says Prof Frank Lobbezoo, a leading researcher on the condition.

And even though bruxism has its negatives (tooth damage, sleep disruption, jaw ache, to name but a few), it's not always the "bad guy", he explains.

"Bruxism is also important for the production of saliva," Lobbezoo says. "Moving the jaw muscles activates the big salivary glands. It cleans the mouth, it protects the teeth and it's vital for digestion."

Some studies also suggest that chewing can help with cognition.

"We know this in animals, and our preliminary research is showing it in humans," he says. "By working our jaw muscles we are stimulating blood flow to the brain."

But teeth grinding can also cause chronic pain, which can have a huge impact on your daily life.

Dentist Riaz Yar, a specialist in prosthodontics, treats patients struggling with the effects of severe bruxism - worn, cracked and fractured teeth, and dental work that keeps failing. Many also arrive with chronic jaw or facial pain and report poor sleep, all of which need assessing in their own right, he says, rather than simply being blamed on the grinding.

In the past, Yar says, teeth grinding was considered simply a mechanical problem of the jaw, but now there is strong evidence that it is much more complex. It's a "biopsychosocial issue", he says, driven by the brain and nervous system and shaped by the whole person.

"We take into account their sleep patterns, their diet, their weight, the amount they exercise, what medication they might be taking and we assess for signs of sleep disorders," he says. "Many factors can contribute to a patient grinding their teeth, so addressing the condition requires a multidisciplinary approach."

How best to tackle it? These things might help:

Mouthguard to wear at night to protect your teeth

If linked to sleep apnoea, devices such as a CPAP machine or a mandibular advancement device (MAD) to help keep the airway open

Lifestyle changes to help reduce stress and improve sleep such as exercise, cutting down on alcohol, stopping smoking and eating healthier

Along with muscle-relaxing injections, Ella says she is also meditating to try to reduce her anxiety and free herself from the tension she regularly carries.

"Having treatment has transformed my life," Ella says, "now I want to try and figure out the root cause."

articles.title: Drag Race co-creator Fenton Bailey speaks out after BBC axe
articles.summary: The BBC is cutting the show because of financial pressures, sparking discussion about LGBTQ+ representation on TV.
articles.body:
The co-creator of Drag Race has said there is a "crisis of representation" on TV, following the BBC's decision to axe the UK edition of the show.

Speaking exclusively to BBC News, Fenton Bailey said he did not believe there was a "hidden agenda" behind the decision, but feared "vulnerable communities are going to be even more vulnerable".

The move led viewers to raise concerns about the corporation's on-screen representation, after it also cancelled two LGBTQ+ dating shows.

A spokesperson for the BBC said the decision was down to "significant financial pressures", as it attempts to make £500m of savings.

Other shows being cancelled include Celebrity Mastermind, Blankety Blank and Live at the Apollo, and more than 500 job losses have also been announced.

World of Wonder (WOW) announced future series of Drag Race UK, including a new All Stars version, will be broadcast exclusively on the company's own streamer, WOW Presents Plus.

BBC News spoke to Bailey, screenwriters, TV critics and former Drag Race contestants about the move and what it means for on-screen representation.

When Drag Race UK launched in 2019, co-creator Fenton Bailey, who was born in Portsmouth but now lives in Los Angeles, said working with the national broadcaster felt like a "very special homecoming" for his production company, WOW.

The US version of the show, co-created by RuPaul Charles, Bailey and his business partner Randy Barbato, had been on air for more than 10 years and was a runaway success, with dozens of Emmy awards and an international following.

Fans were eagerly awaiting a UK series to showcase the unique British style of drag. Now, eight series and three spin-offs later, the programme will stop broadcasting on the BBC after the current series ends.

"Even at the best of times, queer culture is vulnerable and you can't take anything for granted," Bailey told BBC News. "Just because a door opened yesterday doesn't mean it won't be slammed shut the next."

BBC News understands discussions to renew the BBC's deal with the show lasted months, with producers hopeful an agreement could be reached, but talks ultimately failed due to the scale of the savings the corporation is trying to make.

Bailey said it was a sign of the "horrible financial situations" broadcasters are currently facing.

"The team at the BBC are amazing and so passionate about the show, this is not an easy thing for any of the people I interacted with, or something they wanted to do," he added.

Drag Race UK was consistently one of BBC Three's most popular offerings, but according to Barb Audiences data, while average viewing figures for the series rose between 2022 and 2024, overall they've fallen around 15% over the past four years, against a backdrop of declining TV viewing figures across the board.

Bailey said the figures "haven't plummeted," but had instead fallen in line with other terrestrial TV shows, and said the number of viewers watching on social media had risen "because that's where the audience has gone."

Following the announcement, some viewers speculated the show could be acquired by another UK broadcaster, but Bailey suggested the show's creators may prefer to go it alone.

"We love partnerships, but in this particular moment, having the freedom to make the show the way we want may be preferable to getting into bed with another broadcaster and potentially be in the same situation a few more seasons down the road."

A BBC spokesperson said: "As the BBC continues to navigate significant financial pressures and deliver the savings required of us, we have had to make some very difficult choices, none of which have been taken lightly."

'It feels like the drawbridge is pulling up'

Scott Bryan, TV critic and author of Out Now: A Queer History of Modern Television, says the move is indicative of just how severe the financial pressures facing broadcasters have become.

"I can imagine Drag Race is an expensive show to make," Bryan told the BBC, "I can see the pressures the BBC are under, but it's rather concerning in regards to queer storytelling.

"You see LGBTQ+ lives reflected on soaps and primetime dramas much more casually, but there still needs to be shows specifically catering to a queer audience, and it feels like very quickly the drawbridge is pulling up."

Earlier this year the BBC announced LGBTQ+ dating shows I Kissed a Boy and I Kissed a Girl were also being cancelled. The corporation said at the time that it was "exceptionally proud" of the shows, but they had to make "difficult choices in light of our funding challenges".

Author and screenwriter Juno Dawson says viewers have begun to notice a "pattern".

She said: "I think that's why perhaps eyebrows have been raised, because Drag Race hasn't been cancelled in isolation. A couple of other LGBTQ+ shows have gone as well.

"It's a shame this is happening at the BBC, because commercial channels don't necessarily have an obligation to represent all the communities in the UK, but the BBC does and it's supposed to represent all of us, including LGBTQ+ people."

The BBC recently announced Smoggie Queens, which features predominantly LGBTQ+ characters, would be renewed for a third series, and it represents the community elsewhere through storylines in shows including Mr Loverman, Amandaland, Vigil and EastEnders.

A recent report from GLAAD, an American advocacy organisation, found film representation had fallen for a third consecutive year and more than 200 LGBTQ+ TV characters would disappear from screens in 2026 because of cancellations, endings or limited-run series.

While similar figures for the UK aren't collated, Dawson fears a shrinking television industry in the UK will make it harder for commissioners to make LGBTQ+ stories.

"So many of my personal shows have gotten right up to green light, but for lots of different reasons, different commissioners - not just at the BBC - have decided to back away.

"Nobody is ever going to say to you 'it's because it was too niche', but all I can keep doing is writing television that feels true to me and represents me and my life."

'You come for the sparkles… but you're dealing with important topics'

While Drag Race is known for its camp humour and glamour, most episodes also tackled serious topics, with contestants opening up about everything from non-binary and trans identities to substance abuse and the realities of living with HIV.

"There's something very clever about Drag Race," Dawson said, "because you come for the sequins and the sparkles, but actually under its surface, you're dealing with really big, heavy and important topics."

Kate Butch, who competed on season five of Drag Race UK and on spin-off UK vs the World, told the BBC they fear a move away from a public service broadcaster could impact the show's ability to reach audiences with "important" messages.

"It's great the show is going to carry on and shine a spotlight on the amazing drag artistry the UK has to offer," they said, "but I do mourn the possibility of someone maybe just flicking through the channels and randomly finding it."

Butch told BBC News that the show coming off the BBC may also bring some positive changes to the programme - including the possibility of prize money and sponsorships.

"It's a lot of effort to go on Drag Race, a lot of investment and emotional labour," they added, "so I hope the audience follows and keeps supporting the queens."

Fenton Bailey says he's excited about the show's future on its own streaming platform.

"We may not have the resources that the BBC has, but the spirit of Drag and RuPaul's Drag Race is about making something out of nothing," he told the BBC.

"As a community we can survive and thrive in less than optimal conditions.

articles.title: Five night sky events to look forward to this autumn
articles.summary: From meteor showers to a November supermoon, there are a number of impressive sights to behold in the autumn night sky.
articles.body:
Autumn brings longer nights to the northern hemisphere, offering more opportunities to get outside and look up at the night sky.

There is plenty to look out for over the coming months, from impressive meteor showers to dazzling star clusters.

The series of spectacles begins with the Pleiades as the autumn nights draw in.

It will be followed by the impressive Orionid meteor shower in late October, and a planetary parade, the Leonid meteor shower and a supermoon in November.

As the nights lengthen through autumn, one of the most recognisable star clusters in the night sky becomes increasingly prominent.

The Pleiades, also known as the Seven Sisters, is a cluster of young stars around 440 light years from Earth.

Despite its name, most people can see around six stars with the naked eye, although many more become visible through binoculars or a telescope.

Look towards the east during autumn evenings, where the Pleiades can be found in the constellation Taurus.

The Orionid meteor shower is active from early October into November, reaching its peak around 21 October.

Twice each year, Earth passes through trails of dust and debris left behind by Halley's comet. As these tiny particles enter Earth's atmosphere at high speed, they heat up and produce the streaks of light we see as meteors.

The Orionids appear to radiate from the constellation Orion, which gives the shower its name.

For the best chance of seeing them, find somewhere dark and away from artificial lights and allow your eyes time to adjust.

Early risers could be treated to a gathering of Mercury, Venus, Mars and Jupiter around 14 November.

All four planets will be above the horizon before sunrise, although some will be easier to spot than others.

Mercury will be particularly challenging because it remains low in the sky and close to the glare of the rising sun.

Venus and Jupiter, meanwhile, are among the brightest objects in our night sky and should be much easier to pick out.

Another meteor shower arrives later in November, with the Leonids expected to peak around 17 November.

The Leonids can travel at about 70km per second as they enter the Earth's atmosphere, making them some of the fastest meteors visible from Earth.

Under ideal, dark sky conditions, around 10 to 15 Leonids an hour can be visible at the shower's peak, although the actual number seen will depend on weather, light pollution and the brightness of the Moon.

They get their name from the constellation Leo, from which the meteors appear to radiate.

The best time to look is generally after midnight and before dawn, when Leo is higher in the sky.

November's full moon is known as the Beaver Moon. The name is thought to come from the time of year when beavers were particularly active, preparing their lodges and storing food ahead of winter.

It will also be a supermoon, reaching full phase on 24 November.

A supermoon occurs when a full Moon is relatively close to Earth, making it appear slightly larger and brighter.

The November supermoon is also the first of a run of four full Moons which can be classed as supermoons, running through to February 2027.

Be sure to make the most of your autumn skywatching by checking the weather first on the BBC Weather app or online.

articles.title: Houthis called us to say they don't want to fight US: Trump
articles.summary: Middle East News: President Donald Trump said Iran-backed Houthis have asked the US to abstain from targeting the militant group, as a worsening clash with Saudi Arabia.
articles.body: President Donald Trump said Iran-backed Houthis have asked the US to abstain from targeting the militant group, as a worsening clash with Saudi Arabia inflames tensions in the Middle East. "The Houthis called us, and they don't want to fight with us," Trump told reporters during a Saturday meeting in Dublin with Irish Prime Minister Micheal Martin."They don't want us to go after them," and "they would much prefer not having us involved," he added.Trump's comments come amid intensifying fighting between the Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni forces, including attacks on energy facilities in the region and missile launches on southwestern Saudi Arabia.A drone attack on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline resulted in some injuries and damage that was being assessed, the Saudi foreign ministry said without detailing the impact on exports.US President Donald Trump, visiting Ireland to attend a golf tournament at one of his resorts, said Iran was probably to blame. "I think they are, probably they are," Trump told reporters in Dublin when asked if Iran was responsible for the attack on the vital oil conduit.Washington now faces a dilemma over whether to help the Saudis fight the Houthis, risking further expansion of the war. Saudi Arabia's de facto ruler, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, phoned Trump on Thursday and asked for US military help fighting the Houthis, Reuters reported, citing three sources. They said the prince was told that Washington would not intervene directly for now but would help with intelligence. Trump confirmed on Saturday that he had spoken to the crown prince, and said the Houthis had also phoned his administration and asked Washington not to become directly involved in the conflict.Houthis said on Saturday that they had freed more than 200 of their members detained by Saudi-backed pro-govt forces in areas they captured in recent days. The Houthis had already controlled large parts of northern Yemen, including the major cities of Sanaa and Hodeida, before making dramatic advances last week.Iran describes the Houthis as an ally but publicly denies giving them military direction. articles.summary: Os suecos comparecerão às urnas neste domingo (13) para eleições gerais que prometem ser fortemente acirradas.
articles.body:
Homem caminha diante de cartaz do Partido Democrata da Suécia, em 11 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Denis Balibouse/ Reuters

Após uma campanha dominada por uma população mais empobrecida e em um contexto de segurança cada vez mais tenso, os suecos comparecerão às urnas neste domingo (13) para eleições gerais que prometem ser fortemente acirradas.

➡️ Durante vários meses, tudo parecia decidido: as pesquisas apontavam a ampla vantagem do bloco de oposição do centro e da esquerda , liderada pelos social-democratas de Magdalena Andersson. Nas últimas semanas, no entanto, a coalizão de centro-direita do primeiro-ministro, Ulf Kristersson, reduziu a diferença. Segundo analistas, o resultado da votação pode ser decidido por uma margem estreita .

Kristersson é apoiado pelo partido anti-imigração Democratas da Suécia (SD).

"Ainda há um pouco de suspense", destacou Jan Teorell, cientista político da Universidade de Estocolmo. As três pesquisas mais recentes mostram o bloco de esquerda e de centro com quase 50% das intenções de voto, contra 47% para as quatro legendas de direita.

Eleitor deposita cédula em urna em votação antecipada em Estocolmo, na Suécia, em 11 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Denis Balibouse/ Reuters

O bloco de direita prometeu continuar com a política de combate à criminalidade , ao mesmo tempo em que endurece as medidas na área de imigração .

Mas o lema, que permitiu sua chegada ao poder em 2022, enfrenta dificuldades atualmente para gerar o mesmo entusiasmo, segundo Teorell.

Kristersson "chegou ao poder com um programa focado, em particular, no combate à criminalidade e na redução dos preços da energia. A criminalidade e os preços da gasolina diminuíram e, portanto, estes temas já não estão entre as principais preocupações dos eleitores", explicou o cientista político.

Mas, em um país em que as desigualdades não param de crescer e o poder de compra da população diminiu, a esquerda anunciou a intenção de aumentar os impostos sobre os bancos e sobre as rendas mais elevadas para investir em saúde e educação, além de uma proposta de apoio financeiro às famílias .

"Acho que a Suécia mudou e que está muito mais dividida. É necessário melhorar o sistema de saúde e a proteção social", declarou à agência de notícias AFP Hanna Justine Hallbom, de 46 anos, que trabalha na indústria da moda.

Para a líder dos social-democratas, o desafio é determinar "que tipo de país a Suécia deveria ser".

A escolha é entre "uma Suécia onde as pessoas têm trabalho e onde podemos melhorar nosso modelo de proteção social e um país completamente diferente, com um governo dominado pelos Democratas da Suécia, um partido de extrema direita fundado por neonazistas", declarou Magdalena Andersson à AFP durante um comício.

Esta legenda superou, em 2022, o partido de Kristersson para se tornar a segunda força política do país, com quase 20% dos votos.

Em caso de uma nova vitória do bloco de direita, os Democratas da Suécia, anti-imigração, esperam entrar no governo pela primeira vez em sua história e não apenas apoiá-lo, como fizeram durante quatro anos.

O partido exige ministérios desta vez. O primeiro-ministro em fim de mandato prometeu alguns, em particular a pasta da Imigração.

Alguns dias antes das eleições de 13 de setembro, a fundação Expo, que documenta a evolução da extrema direita sueca, revelou que uma funcionária dos SD no Parlamento compartilhou propaganda pró-Rússia diversas vezes .

Ulf Kristersson, que sobreviveu a uma série de escândalos durante seu mandato, reagiu de maneira enérgica.

"Estamos em plena guerra na Europa", declarou ao jornal Aftonbladet. "Não podemos ter no Parlamento pessoas que divulgam discursos pró-Rússia".

articles.title: Vilarejo reúne variedade, estoque e atendimento para cada etapa da obra | G1

articles.summary: Estrutura completa permite que clientes e profissionais encontrem soluções para diferentes fases da obra em um só lugar.
articles.body:
Uma obra envolve muito mais do que escolher bons materiais. Cada etapa exige planejamento, disponibilidade de produtos e orientação para que as decisões tomadas no início do projeto façam sentido até a entrega dos últimos acabamentos. Por isso, reunir variedade, estoque e atendimento especializado em um único lugar tem se tornado um diferencial importante para quem constrói ou reforma.

À medida que os projetos se tornam mais personalizados, cresce também a necessidade de comparar produtos, entender aplicações e avaliar quais materiais atendem melhor às características de cada ambiente. A possibilidade de concentrar essas escolhas em uma única empresa reduz deslocamentos, facilita a compatibilização entre diferentes itens e contribui para uma obra mais organizada.

A variedade de produtos permite que diferentes etapas da obra sejam planejadas em um único lugar — Foto: Acervo Vilarejo

Com mais de 3 mil opções de produtos , a Vilarejo reúne revestimentos, porcelanatos, pedras naturais, louças, metais, tintas, iluminação, acabamentos e acessórios para atender desde pequenas reformas até projetos completos. Esse portfólio permite que clientes e profissionais encontrem soluções compatíveis entre si, mantendo unidade estética e funcionalidade ao longo da obra.

Outro diferencial está na estrutura logística. A empresa conta com mais de 350 mil metros quadrados de revestimentos em estoque , centro de distribuição com 48 mil metros quadrados , frota própria e entregas frequentes para mais de 50 cidades, contribuindo para que o cronograma da obra seja mantido com mais segurança.

Estoque robusto, centro de distribuição e frota própria reforçam a capacidade de atendimento da Vilarejo — Foto: Acervo Vilarejo

Além da disponibilidade dos materiais, a experiência de compra é acompanhada por um atendimento consultivo. A equipe auxilia na comparação entre produtos, esclarece dúvidas sobre aplicações e oferece apoio na especificação dos materiais. Para compras realizadas nas lojas, clientes também contam com projetistas internos, sem custo adicional, que ajudam na paginação e na organização das escolhas antes do início da instalação.

Construir ou reformar exige decisões em diferentes momentos. Ter acesso a uma estrutura preparada para atender todas essas etapas permite que o foco permaneça no desenvolvimento do projeto, com mais tranquilidade do planejamento à execução.

articles.body:
A Lotofácil da Independência 2026 terá um prêmio estimado em R$ 300 milhões . O concurso especial, de número 3780, será sorteado nesta terça-feira (15), às 11h, em horário diferente do habitual dos concursos regulares da Lotofácil.

Uma das principais características da Lotofácil da Independência é que o prêmio principal não acumula. Caso não haja nenhuma aposta com os 15 números sorteados, o valor destinado à faixa principal será distribuído entre os ganhadores da faixa seguinte, conforme as regras da modalidade.

A Lotofácil da Independência é realizada anualmente em setembro e chega, em 2026, à sua 15ª edição.

A Lotofácil deixa de ter os concursos regulares para dar espaço ao concurso especial da Independência. A partir de 4 de setembro, as apostas passaram a ser feitas exclusivamente para a edição especial.

Assim, quem quiser participar da Lotofácil da Independência 2026 terá um período específico para registrar o jogo. As apostas podem ser feitas até as 10h do dia 15 de setembro.

Como apostar na Lotofácil da Independência?

Para participar, o apostador precisa escolher entre 15 e 20 números, dentre os 25 disponíveis no volante da Lotofácil. A aposta simples, com 15 dezenas, custa R$ 3,50.

É possível fazer o jogo nas lotéricas, pelo portal Loterias Caixa ou pelo aplicativo Loterias Caixa. Também estão disponíveis opções como Surpresinha, quando os números são escolhidos aleatoriamente pelo sistema, e Teimosinha.

articles.body: Candace Owens has once again put her strained relationship with Erika Kirk under the spotlight. A post circulating on social media features Owens discussing Charlie Kirk’s death, Turning Point USA and what she describes as a betrayal of the late conservative activist. Her comments, made during an interview with Stephen A. Smith, have drawn attention because of the pointed accusations she directed at Charlie’s widow.Candace Owens calls Charlie Kirk’s wife his “biggest betrayer”The image shows Owens speaking into a microphone during the interview, where the conversation turned sharply toward her views on Charlie Kirk’s legacy and the direction of Turning Point USA.Owens said she initially believed the organization would help her seek answers surrounding Charlie’s death. Instead, she claims the experience left her deeply disappointed.“I was totally under the belief that Turning Point USA would be helping me trying to get answers. So I was in for a surprise.”She then explained why she believes Charlie was betrayed, arguing that her concerns extend beyond the organization itself.“You know, I do hold the belief and express the belief that Charlie was betrayed. And I think he's betrayed every single day, by the way, with the messaging and the partnerships and the direction that Turning Point is going.”The discussion became even more personal when Owens was asked who she considered the biggest betrayer.“Who's the biggest betrayer? Who's the biggest betrayer? Is it the president? Is it Turning Point USA?”Her answer was Erika, Charlie’s wife. Owens framed her opinion through her Catholic understanding of marriage.“It would be his wife, because that's a sacrament. A marriage is a sacrament, in my view, as a Catholic.”Owens went on to make several serious claims about Erika’s conduct and the direction of Turning Point USA. Those statements are Owens’ allegations and have not been independently established by the material provided.Owens details her fallout with Erika KirkOwens also claimed that she once had a friendly relationship with Erika and had supported Charlie’s relationship with her. She said that changed after Charlie’s death.“I met my husband and went into la-la land. And so we've always been kind to each other.”She added that she had encouraged Charlie to take the relationship seriously and said she had messages showing her support.“I've always been friendly with her and always, beyond anything else, supportive of Charlie and said, you should get serious about her.”According to Owens, she tried to offer help after Charlie died, believing Erika would want to investigate what happened.“And when Charlie passed away, I was incredibly supportive. I asked Andrew to give her my number, how I could help in any way.”Owens said she later felt that expectation was misplaced.“Like I said, I was operating under the delusion that she would be interested in exploring and wanting to get to the bottom of what happened to her husband. And I was wrong. I was proven wrong.”She further alleged that people connected to the organization began targeting her after employees were dismissed.“And then I got to see, as they started firing people, that from the very beginning, they knew that I was going to be a problem.”Owens concluded by describing the relationship as permanently changed.“So yeah, definitely not a friend of hers today, if that's the question.”The comments have added another dramatic chapter to the public dispute, with Owens continuing to challenge the people and institutions surrounding Charlie Kirk’s legacy.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Investigators rule out attack in French train derailment
articles.summary: Investigators have ruled out an attack as the cause of a train derailment in north-western France that left more than 40 people injured. Rouen public prosecu...
articles.body:
Investigators have ruled out an attack as the cause of a train derailment in north-western France that left more than 40 people injured.

Further questioning on Sunday is expected to focus on how a section of rail came to be on the tracks, according to reports.

Of the 44 people injured, most had already been discharged from hospital by Saturday, with an 18-year-old woman seriously injured but improving.

Rouen public prosecutor Sébastien Gallois said on Saturday evening that there was so far "no indication of a malicious act carried out with the deliberate intention of derailing the train, and certainly not of an attack," according to several French media reports.

Further questioning on Sunday is expected to focus on how a section of rail came to be on the tracks, the reports said. Several French politicians had previously suggested the incident could have been an attack or another criminal act.

The regional train, carrying around 180 passengers, struck an object on Friday evening while travelling between Rouen and Caen. Five carriages derailed and one overturned.

Initial reports said investigators were looking into the possibility of a deliberate act after a section of rail was found on the tracks.

Of the 44 people injured, most had already been discharged from hospital by Saturday, according to media reports.

An 18-year-old woman was seriously injured, although her condition has since improved, the reports said.

Emergency services deployed in large numbers to the scene, with more than 130 firefighters, 50 police officers and 80 vehicles involved in the response.

articles.title: They lost their jobs after posting about Charlie Kirk, but some have no regrets
articles.summary: Some people fired in the wake of Kirk's assassination have won big settlements from employers, others have had to start over from scratch.
articles.body:
In September 2025, Gerald Bourguet felt he was finally living his dream life: he and his wife had bought a house with a pool, they had just welcomed a baby boy, and he was writing about professional men's basketball as his full-time job.

But all of that changed after he made a series of online posts critical of the late conservative activist Charlie Kirk hours after he was fatally shot on 10 September, while speaking on the campus of Utah Valley University.

In the posts, Bourguet described Kirk as an "evil man" and suggested he had dedicated his life to hateful causes. He also criticised Kirk's supporters saying they had not been vocal about school shootings.

"I had seen the way that people were talking about this person - kind of eulogising him and lionising him and it bothered me based on a lot of the things that he had said," Bourguet told the BBC.

Kirk, who founded Christian youth organisation Turning Point USA, was a divisive figure in US politics. For many on the political right, he was charismatic and had a unique skill in making conservative ideas appeal to young people. But for his opponents, his comments on a large swathe of issues from race to immigration, gun control and gender identity were deeply offensive.

Screenshots of Bourguet's critical posts went viral quickly. He was fired from his job, his address was exposed online, and he began receiving threatening text messages, he said. Concerned for their safety, the family fled the state with their four-month-old. They returned months later to sell the house and permanently relocated.

A year later, he says he doesn't regret what he said, but acknowledged: "My life will never be the same after this".

"At age 35, I am having to start over in a lot of respects… I wouldn't wish this on my worst enemy," Bourguet said from his new location, which the BBC agreed not to disclose.

PHNX Sports, Bourguet's former employer, did not respond to the BBC's request for comment.

Bourguet was one of hundreds fired or disciplined over critical comments of Kirk after his death. While some of those who have lost their jobs have been reinstated or received restitution - sometimes in the millions - others like Bourguet have had to rebuild from scratch.

In the aftermath of Kirk's assassination, most people kept their feelings to themselves, or shared them with close friends.

But on polarised social media, people rushed to laude, or denounce, the controversial activist. Some called the criticisms, posted hours after his death, tasteless. But others called for swift action, arguing they were callous, mocking, and could even incite further violence.

Laura Loomer, an influential right-wing commentator with nearly 2 million followers on X, warned Kirk's critics to "prepare to have your whole future professional aspirations ruined".

The push for punishment also came from the highest levels of US government.

"When you see someone celebrating Charlie's murder, call them out," Vice-President JD Vance said days after the assassination. "And hell, call their employer," he added.

White House spokesperson Davis Ingle told the BBC: "Anyone who engages in or endorses political violence or assassination culture must be condemned in the harshest terms possible."

Critics on the left said there was a difference between criticism of Kirk and celebrating his death. Some accused these conservative leaders of hypocrisy, as many had previously bemoaned the rise of "cancel culture" – where people who voice controversial opinions face severe consequences at work and socially.

"Cancel culture can be good, it's bad when it's applied in the wrong ways," Jordan Pace, a Republican member of the South Carolina House of Representatives, told the BBC. "If you are someone who celebrates political assassinations and the murder of an innocent man with two young children in a way that many people did, then yeah, that's an appropriate way for society to function, to shame those people."

Pace had previously called for defunding universities in his state if they didn't take actions against employees who made comments about Kirk. One of his posts was re-shared by US President Donald Trump.

Across the nation, some employers – private and public – acted swiftly to the pressure campaign. Reliable figures on the number of people fired or disciplined are hard to come by, but a Reuters tally last November found more than 600 instances. It is likely an under-count because not all cases received national or local press attention.

The specific actions that led to these disciplinary decisions run the gamut. In Tennessee, anthropology professor Tamar Shirinian was suspended and later fired for a Facebook comment saying "the world is better off" without Kirk.

A Delta Air Lines flight attendant was fired after posting "good riddance" in response to Kirk's killing. Office Depot supply store fired an employee for refusing to serve a customer who had wanted to print flyers for a Kirk vigil. Delta Air Lines declined to comment. Office Depot did not respond to a request for comment.

Others were disciplined even if they did not make any direct comments about Kirk or his death. Darren Michael, a theatre professor in Tennessee, was fired after he posted a screenshot of a news article from 2023, that covered Kirk's controversial speech on gun control. In the article, Kirk is quoted saying protecting citizens' rights to own guns was worth it even if it led to some gun deaths every year.

Florida's Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission fired biologist Brittney Brown after she reposted a meme that also satirised Kirk's position on gun violence in light of his own shooting.

"I was absolutely gutted," Brown said about her firing to the BBC. "It was like the entire world just completely flipped on its head in a moment."

Lawsuits have yielded big pay outs for those fired

In the year since Kirk's killing, dozens of lawsuits have been filed across the country by people fired for their comments about the activist, arguing their terminations violated their rights to free speech. The suits have led to substantial pay outs in some cases.

Brown agreed to a $485,000 (£355,000) financial settlement – about 12 times Brown's annual salary.

Darren Michael was reinstated by the Austin Peay State University and in January, the school agreed to pay him $500,000 to settle legal claims. The school did not respond to a request for comment.

In the largest settlement reviewed by the BBC, the University of Tennessee agreed to pay $1.9m to resolve a lawsuit brought by anthropologist Tamar Shirinian, over her "better off" comment. As part of the settlement, she will not be reinstated and has agreed not to reapply for future positions at the school.

Recently, an arbitrator ordered The Washington Post to rehire, with back pay, opinion journalist Karen Attiah, who was fired for her online posts that said in part she was not going to engage in "performative mourning for a white man that espoused violence".

Several other lawsuits remain pending, the BBC found.

Most of the legal actions have been pursued by employees of government institutions, or unionised workers, who have some free-speech protections.

But in the US, most private sector employees work under "at-will" contracts, which means they can be can be fired without reason.

Even those who have scored some victories don't see it as a win.

"All I wanted was my job back," biologist Brown said. "How much taxpayer money did they waste on this when I barely made $40,000 a year? So no, it does not feel like justice."

Shirinian told the BBC she too had wanted to return to her job but felt a legal case could be a lengthy affair.

"I took a settlement because this allows me to move on with my life," she told the BBC. "The one small regret that I have is that I will not see my day in court and justice will not be served in that way. But I think that the number of the settlement actually speaks to that anyway."

The University of Tennessee and Florida's Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission did not respond to the BBC's request for comment.

As an at-will employee at a private company, Bourguet is unlikely to prevail in a lawsuit challenging his dismissal. A year on, he said he has struggled to find work. The new state he lives in has a professional basketball team, but he believes the ordeal has made him unemployable in the small world of sports writers. Instead, he's started his own podcast, although he doubts he can earn enough through it to pay the bills.

"I have accepted that that life is over and that I need to start a new one." Leaving the country is now on the table, he said.

Despite the huge personal and professional costs, those who spoke to the BBC said after months of reflection, they did not regret their actions.

"I have a right to say what I want to say," Brown said. "They are the ones who should have the regrets, not me," she said referring to her former employer.

Shirinian apologised to the university days after her suspension. She told the BBC her comment was "an emotional outburst" that was not intended to be public and that she regretted the tone used.

"I don't regret the sentiment, however" she said, adding "the sentiment was that I am not sad. And I refuse to be made to feel like I have to be sad that someone who was so hateful was killed".

Bourguet also said he does not regret his comments although he has conflicting thoughts about its consequences.

"I don't regret that line of thinking because I think it's important to push back on things that are steeped in hatred," he said, referring to Kirk's political message.

"I don't regret what I said. I don't regret the way that I said it. I do regret the ripple effects that came from it and the way that they impacted me, my career, my family, and my son."

articles.title: ‘Slipped and fell’ on saleswoman, then kissed her twice: Mumbai man gets 1-year jail
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Ruling that a natural reaction to a fall does not involve kissing the victim, a sessions court convicted and sentenced to one year rigorous im.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Ruling that a natural reaction to a fall does not involve kissing the victim, a sessions court convicted and sentenced to one year rigorous imprisonment a 34-year-old cleaner who claimed he ac­cidentally “slipped and fe­ll” onto a saleswoman at a Borivli (W) mall be­fore forcibly kissing her twice last year.In a trial that lasted only 2 months, dismissing the defence, the court found Ritesh Armulla guilty of using criminal force and making unwelcome physical contact with explicit sexual overtures.“Even for the sake of arg­ument, if it is considered a pe­r­son slipped and fell on an­ot­h­er person, the natural re­ac­ti­on would be different fr­om the person kissing the person on whom he fell,” judge said.‘Enough proof that act was intentional’The offences are covered under Sections 74, assault or use of criminal force against a woman with intent to outrage, or knowing it is likely to outrage, her modesty, and 75, sexual harassment, of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.Additional Sessions Judge P A Sane said the victim’s evidence was “convincing” and not disbelievable. “There is nothing coming on record as to why the victim will depose against the accused. Moreover, it is coming on record that she did not know the accused before the incident. So there is no possibility that she would falsely involve the accused in this case,” the judge held.This is one of the few convictions since the BNS replaced the IPC.The court sentenced Armulla to one year’s RI and a fine of Rs 1,000 under Section 74, and one year’s simple imprisonment and a fine of Rs 500 under Section 75. Both sentences will run concurrently. The judge said there was sufficient reason to believe that the accused intentionally kissed the complainant, made her fall and kissed her again, amounting to outraging modesty by criminal force. He had followed her on the pretext of being shown the washroom and physically contacted her with explicit sexual overtures.The case arose from an incident on Sept 17, 2025, at a mall in Borivli West. The victim, a sales girl at the mall, told the court that around 6 pm she was on duty and walking towards billing counter number 6 after taking a cold drink bottle. A man in a pink shirt approached her and asked where the washroom was. She pointed in that direction, but he repeatedly asked her to show him.According to the prosecution, after she asked him to go ahead, he left briefly and returned. The victim said the accused came from behind, knocked against her, asked her to take him to the washroom and, when she refused and proceeded towards the billing counter, forcibly kissed her, caused her to fall and kissed her again. Staff and other people in the mall caught him. Police were called, and he was taken into custody the same day.The FIR was lodged immediately. Police prepared the spot panchnama, arrested Armulla, recorded statements and collected CCTV footage. The chargesheet was filed on November 11, 2025, and charges were framed on July 4, 2026.The prosecution examined the victim, an eyewitness, the investigating officer and a mall employee linked to the CCTV footage. The victim identified Armulla in court, and the eyewitness supported her account.The defence questioned proof of the CCTV footage, non-examination of a mall official, absence of hash value and intent, claiming any contact may have been accidental. articles.body: A trespasser was stopped at former US Vice President Kamala Harris’ Malibu property Friday night after private security spotted the individual entering the premises, authorities and Harris’ spokesperson said.Harris and her husband, Doug Emhoff, were not at the property at the time, spokesperson Eduardo Negrón said to news agency NewsNation. He added that security personnel present stopped the individual before they could get to the actual house. Negrón also mentioned that Harris and her husband were grateful to the security and law enforcement personnel who responded swiftly.News agency TMZ also spoke with a spokesperson from the Los Angeles county sheriff’s department who confirmed that the Malibu Lost Hills deputies were called to the property around 10.30 pm following a report of a suspicious person. The individual had already been stopped by private security and was outside the property when deputies arrived.The Times had initially reported that deputies were contacted by security after “a woman made it to Harris’ front door” but Negrón told NewsNation that she did not make it that far and was intercepted.Deputies warned the trespasser to leave, and the person left voluntarily without incident, the department said. No arrest was made.Authorities said patrols around the property were being increased as a precaution.Harris and Emhoff bought the Malibu beach house for $8.15 million in December. The purchase had fuelled speculation about Harris’ political plans, including whether she could seek another presidential run in 2028.The incident has also drawn renewed attention to Harris’ security arrangements. Former President Joe Biden had extended Harris’ federal protection beyond the standard six-month period for former vice presidents, but President Donald Trump ended that protection in 2025.California governor Gavin Newsom said the California Highway Patrol would take over security responsibilities for Harris. The cost of the state-funded security detail has not been disclosed.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
