articles.title: Ladakh to host the world’s highest marathon in September with ₹1 crore prize pool; dates, races, key rules and everything travellers need to know
articles.summary: Imagine running through Ladakh’s rugged lan, crossing the Indus River with the Himalayas rising around you and doing it at an altitude where even walk.
articles.body: Imagine running through Ladakh’s rugged lan, crossing the Indus River with the Himalayas rising around you and doing it at an altitude where even walking can feel demanding. That is the challenge awaiting runners at the 13th edition of the Ladakh Marathon, being held in Leh from September 10 to September 13, 2026. Organised by the High Altitude Sports Foundation Ladakh (HASF), the event is officially described as the world’s highest AIMS-certified marathon and has attracted runners from India and abroad.This year, the event has an enhanced total prize pool of ₹1 crore, according to the Ladakh Administration.When and where is the Ladakh Marathon 2026?The four-day event is being staged in and around Leh, Ladakh, with six different running categories spread across September 10 to 13.Silk Route Ultra : The 122-km run is scheduled for September 10Khardung La Challenge : The 72-km race is on September 11.Run for Fun : The popular 5-km takes place on September 12Flagship Marathon: On September 13, runners will compete in a 42.195-km marathon, 21.0975-km Half Marathon and 11.2-km Run.The full marathon starts from the NDS Memorial Stadium at 6 AM on September 13. The official cut-off time is 6 hours 45 minutes.What’s in for visitors?For visitors, the marathon is also an unusual way to experience Ladakh. The full-marathon route passes through landscapes featuring the Indus, villages and monasteries. The organisers describe the event as an opportunity to run alongside local Ladakhis.RegistrationsRegistrations opened on February 19 and closed on March 23, 2026.Different races have different age and qualification requirements.For September 13, 2026The minimum age is 12 years for the 5-km Run for Fun14 for the 11.2-km Run16 for the Half Marathon18 for the full Marathon20 for the Khardung La Challenge24 for the Silk Route Ultra₹1 crore prize poolThe biggest draw this year is the ₹1 crore overall prize pool, which the Ladakh Administration announced while launching the official marathon jersey in August. The administration said the enhanced prize pool contributed to unprecedented interest, with registrations reaching nearly 10,000 runners, compared with 6,521 participants the previous year.Prize money is offered across the five timed races, for both men and women, covering the overall top three and top three veterans. The 5-km Run for Fun is not a timed race.Prize entitlements are based on chip time, with winners' names announced provisionally on race day before final verification. The organisers state that prize money will be transferred to winners' bank accounts within 30 to 60 working days after the event, following ratification of the results.The most important rule: acclimatise before runningLeh is located at high altitude, and the organisers strongly emphasise acclimatisation before race day.For the Silk Route Ultra and Khardung La Challenge, participants are advised to arrive in Leh at least 15 days before the race.Marathon and Half Marathon participants are advised to arrive at least 10 days in advance,Those taking part in the 11.2-km and 5-km races are advised to arrive at least seven days before their event.A marathon that is also a high-altitude travel experienceThe Ladakh Marathon is unlike a conventional city race. Participants run through an extraordinary Himalayan landscape, while the altitude itself becomes part of the challenge. With six race formats, international recognition and a ₹1 crore prize pool, the 2026 edition has turned Leh into a destination for both serious endurance athletes and running enthusiasts.For those who missed the 2026 registration window, the best approach is to watch the official Ladakh Marathon website for the next edition, study its qualifying requirements and plan the trip around the organisers' acclimatisation recommendations.Looking for trusted parenting advice? articles.title: Pakistani actress Mahira Khan announces second pregnancy at 41 in a stunning white dress, expecting baby with Salim Karim
articles.summary: Mahira Khan has shared some very happy news, and she did it with a picture that feels every bit as beautiful as the moment itself.The actress posted a.
articles.body: Mahira Khan has shared some very happy news, and she did it with a picture that feels every bit as beautiful as the moment itself.The actress posted a photo showing off her baby bump in a flowing white gown, looking calm, elegant and completely at ease. There was no heavy styling or dramatic setup. The soft dress, her pregnancy glow and that one emotional caption said enough.“We make plans and then there is ALLAH’S plan,” Mahira wrote.And within no time, the picture had fans celebrating the actress and her growing family.Mahira lets her baby bump take centre stageFor the special announcement, Mahira chose a long, loose white gown with full sleeves and a soft, almost dreamy feel. The fabric fell naturally around her baby bump, creating a relaxed silhouette instead of trying to disguise it.She kept the overall look simple, too. That worked.With one hand gently resting on her bump, Mahira looked happy and comfortable rather than overly posed. The sheer, soft styling around the dress added to the romantic feel of the photograph without taking attention away from her.It’s the kind of maternity dressing that doesn’t need much else.A very different chapter for MahiraThe pregnancy comes almost three years after Mahira married businessman Salim Karim in October 2023.This will be their first child together and Mahira’s second. She is already a mother to her son, Azlan, whom she shares with her first husband Ali Askari.Mahira's second wedding was a particularly emotional moment for her, with Azlan walking her down the aisle. At the time, she spoke about how special it was to have her son beside her as she began a new chapter.She had once imagined her life being just her and Azlan. So, finding love again and now preparing to welcome another baby marks a pretty big change in the life she had pictured for herself.Mahira has spoken about how different this pregnancy feelsInterestingly, this isn't Mahira's first time talking about how different pregnancy feels at this stage of her life.In an interview with Dawn, the actress said she was 24 when she was pregnant with Azlan. Now 41, she admitted that the experience has been much harder physically and emotionally.“The last time I was pregnant I was 24. I’m 41 now, so I’m literally a different woman … emotionally, physically, in every possible way,” she said.She also spoke about how, at 24, she approached pregnancy with a certain innocence. This time, she knows more, worries more and understands just how much life can change.There has also been the adjustment of stepping back from a life that was already moving at full speed. Mahira has her career, work, travel, routines and a grown-up son. Starting all over again wasn't necessarily something she had imagined for this stage of her life.But perhaps that's exactly what makes her latest announcement feel so personal.“You imagine a lot of things for yourself and for your life, and this wasn’t necessarily one of the things I had imagined at this point,” she said.“But we plan and then God plans, and of course His plans are supreme.”Her latest picture seems to carry that same feeling.No big fashion statement. No elaborate announcement.Just Mahira in white, embracing her baby bump and stepping into a chapter she may not have planned for, but is clearly ready to welcome.Looking for trusted parenting advice? articles.title: Larry Ellison cancels plan to sell $7.5 billion of Oracle stock after Europe has a problem with 'his timing'
articles.summary: Tech News News: ​Larry Ellison has decided to cancel a trading plan a day after disclosing it. This plan would have allowed the Oracle co-founder to sell up to 50 mil.
articles.body: ​Larry Ellison has decided to cancel a trading plan a day after disclosing it. This plan would have allowed the Oracle co-founder to sell up to 50 million shares of the software company. Oracle has now confirmed that Ellison has sold no shares under the arrangement, which was due to remain in place until October 24. The timing has drawn attention because European market-abuse rules would not have allowed an executive to trade during the 30 days before financial results.In a press release, the company wrote, “Larry Ellison, Executive Chair of the Board and Chief Technology Officer, has cancelled his 10b5-1 Plan to sell Oracle stock. No Oracle stock was sold under that plan, and he has no other plans to sell any of his Oracle stock.”​The shares covered by the plan were worth about $8.75 billion when it was adopted on June 22 and are worth about $7.5 billion at the current price, after Oracle's stock fell roughly 16%. This trading plan also drew attention because Oracle had just reported shrinking gross margins, while the company was also increasing the expected cost of its job cuts to $2.8 billion.​Why Larry Ellison cancelled the Oracle stock sale plan​The plan to scrap highlights differences between US and European rules for companies. In the US, executives can set up Rule 10b5-1 plans beforehand. Meanwhile, in Europe, the trading window typically closes before financial results, rather than offering a similar safe harbour as offered in America.​Oracle has taken on significant debt as it expands its infrastructure business, while its shares have fallen roughly 20% this year. In its latest earnings, the company reported a 121% year-over-year increase in cloud infrastructure revenue and exceeded estimates, but also posted shrinking gross margins and raised the expected cost of its job cuts to $2.8 billion. Its shares fell 1.7% after the results.​Ellison controls about 40% of Oracle and is its executive chair and chief technology officer. Selling all 50 million shares under the proposed plan would still have left him with about 1.1 billion shares. The sale was unusual given that, according to FactSet, he has not sold more than 25,000 Oracle shares at a time since the start of the century.​What is a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan in the US​A Rule 10b5-1 Plan is the American way of enabling executives and other insiders to prearrange stock sales. This means an executive may develop the plan when he does not have insider information; the trades are then made according to the set instructions.The plan allows the executive to dispose of shares at times when the decision would raise questions about whether he had access to material, non-public information. The rule was developed in 2000, and the SEC strengthened disclosure requirements in 2022.In Ellison's case, the plan has been publicly disclosed because American regulations require it. However, because no shares were sold before cancelling the plan, no transaction occurred.​Why Europe takes a different approach​European market-abuse rules do not have an equivalent to the US 10b5-1 safe harbour. Under the European Union's Market Abuse Regulation, people discharging managerial responsibilities generally cannot trade in their company's shares during the 30 calendar days before an interim or year-end financial report.​So the European approach closes the trading window instead of letting executives implement a pre-arranged plan that can continue during the restricted period.The disclosure rules are also different. In Europe, regulators focus more on reporting closed transactions than on the intent to set up a trading plan. Company managers must report transactions within three working days of reaching the annual threshold of €5,000.​So a plan that was set out but never executed would not have resulted in the same disclosure in Europe.​Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: Two giant dams changed Europe’s second-longest river. Decades later, scientists found the Danube Delta was being starved of sediment
articles.summary: Europe News: The Danube does not arrive at the Black Sea as it once did. For thousands of years, the river carried enormous quantities of sediment towards its delt.
articles.body: The Danube does not arrive at the Black Sea as it once did. For thousands of years, the river carried enormous quantities of sediment towards its delta, steadily building and reshaping the low-lying landscape where river channels meet lagoons and the sea. That process changed after large-scale engineering works altered the river upstream. Following the construction of the Iron Gates dams, the amount of sediment reaching the lower Danube fell sharply. By the following decades, the delta was no longer receiving enough material to maintain the balance that had helped shape it for millennia. Along parts of the Black Sea coast, erosion began to take a greater role.How the Danube built its delta over 12,000 yearsThe Danube Delta is the product of a very long relationship between flowing water, sediment and the Black Sea. According to the research published in Estuarine, Coastal and Shelf Science, titled ‘Danube River Sediment Input and its Interaction with the North-western Black Sea’, over roughly 12,000 years, material carried downstream accumulated around the river's mouth, allowing the delta to extend and change as channels shifted and new deposits formed.That process depended on a continuing supply from the river. Sediment arriving from upstream could be deposited across the delta, along its shoreline or farther out on the Black Sea shelf.Human intervention altered that pattern. Dams and other engineering works changed the movement of water and sediment through the Danube system, leaving parts of the modern delta with a much smaller supply of the material that had helped create it.How the Iron Gates dams changed the DanubeThe construction of the Iron Gates dam system on the Danube was a major change for the river. After the dams were built, sediment discharge downstream dropped to around 30–40% of its earlier level, as reported in the study.The reduction was not simply a matter of less material moving through the river. Large reservoirs can trap sediment that would otherwise continue downstream. Material settles within the impounded sections rather than travelling towards the delta.For a landscape dependent on a river to keep delivering sediment, the change was significant.The Danube Delta had spent thousands of years gaining land through deposition. With a much smaller sediment supply arriving from upstream, parts of the system were left with less material available to offset the forces continually wearing the coastline away.Where the Danube’s sediment still reaches the seaThe effect became particularly apparent along the delta's seaward edge. The reduced sediment supply contributed to stronger erosional processes along the deltaic coast.The north-western Black Sea shelf can be broadly divided into two contrasting areas. Closer to the Danube, the inner shelf remains strongly influenced by sediment delivered by the river. Farther offshore, the outer shelf is comparatively sediment-starved.That distinction matters because the Danube is not only important for the wetlands and channels that can be seen from the surface. Its sediment has also shaped the seabed beyond the delta.Over time, deposits from the river accumulated across the north-western Black Sea. But the modern sedimentary record indicates that the Danube's deep-sea fan is no longer developing as it did during earlier periods.The delta’s natural sediment cycle has been disruptedDifferent parts of the delta experience different combinations of deposition and erosion. Sediment continues to move through the river and across the coastal zone, while waves, currents and changing water conditions redistribute material.After thousands of years of active growth and reshaping, much of the delta became relatively inactive during the last few decades. Human modifications to the river system were one part of that change.Ten small dams removed to free rivers and reconnect habitatTen obsolete dams on the Kogilnik and Sarata Rivers have been removed within the Danube Biosphere Reserve. The rivers rise in Moldova before reaching the Sasyk Lagoon in Ukraine, and the small Soviet-era barriers had restricted their flow near their mouths for years.Removing those structures was not expected to restore the sediment supply lost at the Iron Gates. It addresses a different problem, lower down in the river network, by reconnecting sections of rivers that had become fragmented.As reported by ELSP, the intervention is about 20 kilometres of river habitat, including areas of flooded meadow. Freer movement of water should allow natural river processes to resume in places where the dams had interrupted them.Fish and wetlands stand to benefitDams can interfere with fish movement as well as altering the physical behaviour of a river. They can interrupt migration routes, change how sediment travels and separate habitats that would otherwise remain connected.The Kogilnik and Sarata removal project intended to reverse some of those effects. Species such as wild carp, frogs and otters are among the wildlife expected to benefit, while the connected river sections should also provide habitat for breeding and migratory birds.For fish, the consequences may extend beyond movement. Improved water flow can help revitalise riverside vegetation and flooded areas that provide spawning habitat.Restoration plans target fish, wetlands and flood resilienceThe dam removals were carried out with input from local communities, and the town council of Tatarbunary approved the project.Fishermen were expected to benefit if fish populations recovered in the connected river sections. Healthier wetlands and more accessible natural areas could also create opportunities for nature-based tourism.Restoring more natural channels and improving water movement can influence how flooding affects surrounding farmland and infrastructure.A second phase of the project was planned around feasibility studies for clearing and restoring channels farther upstream, extending the restoration beyond the locations where the obsolete dams were removed.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Arun Jaitley Stadium pitch report, T20I records and average scores ahead of India vs. Afghanistan three-match series
articles.summary: With India set to be the guests at the Arun Jaitley Stadium as they face Afghanistan on Sunday, here's a look at what they can expect from the stadium.
articles.body:
India is all set to take on Afghanistan in the opening T20I at the Arun Jaitley Stadium on Sunday, September 13.

Shreyas Iyer's side looking to build momentum after a mixed white-ball summer that included series defeats in Ireland and England.

Meanwhile, Afghanistan will be hoping to avenge defeat in the one-off Test at Mullanpur earlier this year. Ibrahim Zadran's side has the perfectly volatile combination of a spin-heavy bowling attack and a batting lineup that's still trying to figure out their place.

With Jasprit Bumrah and Washington Sundar also cleared just this week, India will be keen to prepare mentally for the upcoming Asian Games and New Zealand. The venue will also play a big part in the match.

Arun Jaitley Stadium has hosted only a handful of T20Is despite its status as one of India's most-used grounds across formats, and their most recent appearance produced one of the highest totals ever recorded there when India piled up 209 against Namibia in February 2026.

With Afghanistan's spin-heavy attack expected to test India's top order on a surface that has traditionally favored batters.

The Sporting News brings you the pitch report, key T20I records, and everything you need to know about the ground in the shortest format.

Arun Jaitley Stadium pitch report: Is it a batting or bowling wicket?

The Arun Jaitley Stadium has developed into one of the more batting-friendly surfaces on the Indian T20 circuit, with a flat, true bounce that has increasingly rewarded stroke play in recent years, a shift from its older reputation as a slower, spin-assisted track.

Seamers can still find some early movement under overcast conditions, but spinners remain effective through the middle overs once the surface settles. Dew has become an increasing factor in evening fixtures, generally tilting the balance towards the chasing side in recent matches at the venue.

What is the average T20I score at Arun Jaitley Stadium?

Across 15 T20Is played at the venue, the average first-innings score sits at 149, with sides batting second averaging 132.

A total in the range of 165 to 180 has generally proven competitive, though the ground has produced five scores of 200 or more in just 15 matches, proving just how quickly totals can escalate on a good batting surface.

Highest team total at Arun Jaitley Stadium in T20Is

India holds the record for the highest T20I total at the venue, having posted 221 for 9 against Bangladesh on October 9, 2024, a match India went on to win by 86 runs.

Lowest team total at Arun Jaitley Stadium in T20Is

Namibia owns the unwanted record for the lowest total, having been bowled out for 116 against India in 2026 during the T20 World Cup. India went on to win the game by 93 runs.

Highest individual score at Arun Jaitley Stadium in T20Is

Rohit Sharma and Shikhar Dhawan hold the joint highest individual score in T20Is at the venue, with both scoring 80 runs. Dhawan has a slight advantage, however, scoring his 80 off 52 balls compared to Sharma's 55.

Best bowling figures at Arun Jaitley Stadium in T20Is

UAE's Junai Siddique also has the best bowling figures at the venue after he took five wickets against Canada for just 35 runs during the 2026 T20 World Cup.

Most runs at Arun Jaitley Stadium in T20Is

Ishan Kishan boasts the most runs at the venue, scoring 137 runs across 2 matches at an average of 68.50 at a strike rate of 190. He is followed by Sohaib Khan with 125 runs scored across two matches.

Most wickets at Arun Jaitley Stadium in T20Is

Junaid Sidique from the UAE has the most wickets at the venue, with 7 scalps in 3 matches at the venue.
